summary: Feed s125_double is degraded: 8.4% duplicate packets and 97.2% encrypted bytes exceed NDR tolerance (90%). NDR will waste capacity on duplicates and is blind to most payloads.

findings.root_cause: Almost all traffic (97.2%) is TLS-encrypted with no upstream decryption. NDR requires full payload inspection but receives opaque ciphertext, exceeding its 90% encrypted tolerance.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR cannot inspect payloads for IDS signatures, malware, C2 or data exfiltration; detection coverage drops to metadata-only (JA3, SNI, flow sizes) and most threats will be missed.

recommended_fix.why: Decrypting once at the visibility layer restores cleartext payload to the NDR while keeping keys centralized; selective decrypt (bypass banking/health) maintains privacy and keeps encrypted share below 90%.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is aggregating the same traffic from two SPAN/mirror sources or both sides of a TAP without deduplication - 152 of 1811 packets (8.4%) are exact duplicates, above 5% threshold.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR wastes CPU/storage on duplicate flows, inflates flow counts and alerts, skews analytics and can cause false-positive correlation and missed true positives due to reassembly confusion.

recommended_fix.why: Enabling broker-based deduplication within a 5-10ms window removes SPAN-induced copies before the 10G NDR port, restoring accurate single-copy traffic without loss.
